Short title and commencement

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
LAW REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE,
1972
1. Short title and
commencement.‑(1) This Ordinance may be called the Law Reforms
(Amendment) Ordinance, 1972.
(2) It shall come into force at
once, and shall be deemed to have taken effect on the 14th April 1972.

Amendment of section 3 Ordinance XII of 1972

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
LAW REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE,
1972
2. Amendment of section 3,
Ordinance XII of 1972.‑1n the Law Reforms Ordinance, 1972 (XII of
1972), hereinafter referred to as the said Ordinance, for section 3 the
following shall be substituted and shall be deemed always to have been so
substituted, namely:‑
"3. Appeal to High Court in certain cases.‑(1) An appeal shall lie to
a Bench of two or more Judges of a High Court from a decree passed of final
order made by a Single Judge of that High Court in the exercise of its original
civil jurisdiction:
Provided that no such appeal
shall lie from an order which does not dispose of the whole matter before the
Court.
(2) No appeal shall lie to a
Bench of two or more Judges of a High Court from an order made by a single
Judge of that High Court under clause (2) of Article 201 of the Interim
Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in a matter arising under any
law relating to be rehabilitation and settlement of displaced persons or from
an order so made under such paragraph
(i) of paragraph (b) of that clause.
(3) Nothing contained in this
Ordinance shall be construed as affecting‑---
(a) any appeal under the provisions of the Letters Patent
applicable to a High Court or under section 102 of the Code of Civil Procedure,
1908 (V of 1908), which was pending immediately before the commencement of this
Ordinance ; or
(b) any appeal or petition for
leave to appeal from a decree, judgment or order of a single Judge of a High
Court made to the Supreme Court before the commencement of the Law Reforms
(Amendment) Ordinance, 1972.".

Addition of new section 4 Ordinance XII of 1972

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
LAW REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE,
1972
3. Addition of new section 4, Ordinance X11 of 1972.‑In the said Ordinance, after section
3, substituted as aforesaid, the following new section shall be added, namely:‑,
"4. Computation of period of limitation.‑In
computing the period of limitation for filing an appeal under the provisions of
section 3, the period commencing the
fourteenth of April 1972, or the date of the decree or order against which the
appeal is to be filed, whichever shall be later, and that date of the
commencement of the Law Reforms (Amendment) Ordinance, 1972, shall be
excluded.".

Amendment of schedule  Ordinance  XII of 1972

ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
ORDINANCE XXXIV OF 1972
LAW REFORMS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE,
1972
4. Amendment of the Schedule, Ordinance XII of 1972.‑In the said
Ordinance, in the Schedule,‑
(i) in column 4, in the entries
relating to the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898), in item 128,
after the new section 382‑B, the following new section shall be added,
namely:‑
"382‑C. False or scandalous plea to be considered in passing sentence.---- In passing a sentence on
an accused for any offence, a Court may take into consideration any false or
scandalous plea taken fn defence by him or on his behalf."; and
(ii) for the entries relating
to the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1965 (111 of 1965), the
following shall be substituted and shall be deemed always to have been so
substituted, namely:‑
"In section 22, after
subsection (2), the following new subsection shall be added, namely:‑
(3) No advocate shall appear or
act for any person in any Court or tribunal unless he has been appointed for
the purpose by such person by a document in writing signed by such person or
his recognized agent or some other person duly authorised by him to make such
appointment, and such document has been filed in such Court or tribunal;
Provided that nothing in this
subsection shall apply to‑-----
(a) a Public Prosecutor or any
advocate appointed by the State ; or
(b) an advocate when appearing
on behalf of another advocate entitled to appear and act, if the advocate so
appearing files a memo of appearance;‑
Provided further that an advocate
may be allowed to appear for an accused in custody on his undertaking to file
the document required under this subsection.".
